thread.title: Facebook co-founder raises $40 million for streaming TV service Philo, launches service on Amazon Fire TV and Apple TV

author: Alisha Green
title: Facebook co-founder raises $40 million for streaming TV service Philo, launches service on Amazon Fire TV and Apple TV
text: – Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Jul 11, 2018, 9:44am EDT San Francisco-based Philo is making big moves in the streaming space with $40 million in new funding and launches on Amazon Fire TV and Apple TV. The launches add to the list of places users can watch live and on-demand TV on Philo, which already includes Roku devices, web browsers, and iPhones. Philo, named after inventor of the electronic television Philo Farnsworth, started out as a TV service in college dorms. It expanded in November 2017 to the general public with backing from programmers A&E, AMC, Discovery, Scripps and Viacom. Making Philo available on Amazon Fire TV (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Apple TV (NASDAQ: AAPL) was a top priority following the November launch because a number of people said they wanted to use Philo on more devices, Philo CEO Andrew McCollum told the San Francisco Business Times. “So this was a really important step just to open up the availability of the service to more people,” McCollum said. Now, with $40 million in new funding, Philo will be turning its attention to adding some of the social features it had been planning to launch early this year. McCollum knows the power of online social networks firsthand, too, as a co-founder of social media giant Facebook (NASDAQ: FB). The Series C round of funding for Philo includes support from returning investors with AMC Networks , Discovery and Viacom leading the round. It brings Philo’s total funding to some $91 million. Philo declined to share its valuation. The new funding will also go toward more marketing for Philo to spread awareness about its offerings, McCollum said. Philo declined to share specific numbers or growth rates for users and revenue, but McCollum said subscribers watch an average of more than three hours of content on Philo per day. “It is interesting to see TV still has a lot of relevance for people,” McCollum said. Philo offers 40 TV channels for $16 per month and an additional nine channels for an extra $4. The company has around 40 employees, including a handful in offices in New York and Cambridge, Mass. McCollum said he expects the size of the team to double over the next 12 months. – Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Jul 11, 2018, 9:44am EDT Related Content
